Belarus conditions its higher target on international financeA higher economy-wide reduction target of at least 40 per cent by 2030 is conditional on international financing mechanisms supporting the introduction of best available technologies.Commitment+1 point1 document1 quote

The NDC sets a conditional economy-wide target to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions by at least 40 per cent from the 1990 level by 2030, inclusive of LULUCF. The condition is using international financing mechanisms to introduce best available technologies for emissions reduction; the document does not say that this finance has been secured or allocated.

EnergyEconomy & Transition
Climate policy prioritizes a more efficient economyNational climate policy is being improved and focuses on sustainable development and reducing national energy and carbon intensity; the document describes this policy as underway.Result reported0 points1 document3 quotes

The document says national climate policy is being improved as part of implementing the Paris Agreement, focused on sustainable development and reducing the energy intensity and carbon intensity of the national economy. It reports that targeted state policy on energy saving and production energy efficiency reduced the economy’s carbon intensity almost threefold between 1995 and 2018. It also states that Belarus intends to reduce the economy’s carbon intensity in future. These passages describe policy activity and a reported outcome, but do not specify economic diversification or a just-transition measure.

ClimateNature, Forests & Land
Conditional economy-wide emissions target for 2035A higher 47% reduction target is conditional on maintaining forest and other-ecosystem absorption, international carbon-market access, sanctions relief and external financial, technical and technology support.Commitment+1 point1 document2 quotes

The conditional economy-wide target is to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions by at least 47 percent by the end of 2035 relative to the 1990 base-year level, including the land-use sector. The document states this corresponds to an absolute reduction of 58.15 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent. Conditions include maintaining the achieved absorption capacity of forests and other ecosystems, access to international carbon-market mechanisms, ending international sanctions, and external financial resources, capacity-building, technical assistance and emissions-reduction technology transfer.

Energy
Conditional energy-intensity reduction by 2035Under the stated conditions for the conditional economy-wide emissions goal, Belarus says GDP energy intensity would be reduced by 22–25 percent by 2035 relative to 2010.Commitment+1 point1 document1 quote

The document links the projected reduction in GDP energy intensity to conditions attached to the conditional economy-wide emissions goal. Those conditions include maintaining the achieved absorption capacity of forests and other ecosystems, access to international carbon-market mechanisms, ending the international sanctions regime, and obtaining external financial resources and support for capacity, finance, technical assistance, and technology transfer. The stated energy-intensity reduction is therefore conditional, not an unconditional sector target.

Economy & Transition
Limited capacity to mobilize low-carbon investmentBelarus describes its transition-economy status and comparatively lower per-capita GDP as constraints on additional low-carbon investment, and considers its unconditional emissions target optimal in the current context.Concern0 points1 document1 quote

Belarus identifies itself as a transition economy and says its per-capita GDP is lower than that of most Annex I Parties. It says this limits its ability to mobilize additional investment in low-carbon technologies and innovations, and describes the unconditional 35 per cent emissions-reduction target as optimal in the current socio-economic context. This is a stated constraint, not a diversification or just-transition programme.

    “The Republic of Belarus - an Annex I Party to the Framework Convention - is a transition economy, whose per capita gross domestic product (hereinafter referred to as “GDP”) is lower compared to most Annex I Parties to the Framework Convention. In this regard, the Republic of Belarus has a limited ability to mobilize additional investment in low-carbon technologies and innovations. Thus, the target of ensuring the reduction of emissions by 35 per cent as compared to the 1990 level inclusive of the LULUCF sector is optimal in the current socio-economic context.”
